overall: The AG found the Hopkinton Board of Selectmen violated the Open Meeting Law by giving vague executive session notices and by discussing general compensation policy in executive session, and ordered compliance and release of minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Oct. 21, 2014 notice for an executive session on nonunion contract negotiations was too vague because it did not name the employee.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the October 21, 2014 meeting agenda should have contained Chief Clark's name.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Nov. 18 and Dec. 16, 2014 notices for litigation executive sessions did not name the pending lawsuit.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, the November 18 and December 16, 2014 notices should have stated that the Board planned to discuss the Doe v. Town of Hopkinton lawsuit.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Dec. 2, 2014 litigation executive session notice was too vague, though the Board entered session without discussing litigation.
allegations.key_passage: When a public body does not actually engage in executive session deliberation, the Open Meeting Law is not violated with respect to the sufficiency of the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board improperly convened an executive session under the nonunion negotiations purpose; the Nov. 18, 2014 session discussed broader compensation policy.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding this discussion in executive session.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law

Release the November 18, 2014 executive session minutes to the public within thirty (30) days of receipt of the letter, without redaction or withholding under privilege or Public Records Law exemptions
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Furthermore, because a discussion took place during the November 18, 2014 executive session that lacked a proper purpose, we order the Board to release these executive session minutes to the public within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter.
